name: auth_service.py
summary: Encapsulates user authentication and JWT token generation for the users application.
purpose: To centralize authentication logic, decouple Django views from direct dependencies on Django's auth system and SimpleJWT, and provide a reusable domain service for validating credentials and issuing tokens.
responsibilities: Authenticating user credentials against the User model
Generating and managing JWT access and refresh tokens via SimpleJWT
Handling authentication validation errors and token exceptions
Coordinating User and Profile model interactions during authentication flows
inputs: User and Profile model instances or query filters
outputs: JWT token pairs (access and refresh tokens)
ValidationError or TokenError exceptions on authentication failure
architecture_notes: Implements the Service Layer pattern within a modular Django architecture (backend/apps/users/services). It isolates domain authentication logic from presentation (views/APIs) and infrastructure (Django auth, SimpleJWT), promoting testability and single responsibility. However, direct imports of concrete models (User, Profile) and third-party token libraries couple the service to specific implementations, reducing flexibility for testing and future auth provider changes.
improvements: Introduce abstract repositories or protocols for User and Profile access to reduce direct ORM coupling and improve unit testability
Add structured security logging and audit trails for authentication attempts, successes, and token issuance
Implement brute-force protection or rate-limiting logic, either within the service or via a cross-cutting decorator
Remove redundant imports (e.g., duplicate RefreshToken) and add strict type hints to all public methods
Extract token generation and management into a dedicated TokenService to adhere more strictly to the Single Responsibility Principle
